sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Options and database query
sections.what: Reads the options and runs one query for active quotes with no stored translation, optionally limited to one industry.
sections.why: Limits the work to quotes that may need translating.
sections.watch_out: A quote already in the agent translations file is still checked later, so the list is only as complete as that file.

sections.name: seen
sections.title: Filtering and printing
sections.what: Keeps only quotes detected as non-English that are not already translated or repeated, then prints them as lines or JSON with a count.
sections.why: Likely reason: removes repeats so each phrase is translated once.
sections.watch_out: Repeats are removed by a key built from the quote text, so near-identical quotes can still appear twice depending on how that key is built.

summary: Prints active evidence quotes that look non-English and have no translation yet, so they can be translated and added to the translations file.
purpose: Helps the team find which quotes still need a translation.
why: Likely reason: English-speaking readers need translations of non-English quotes.
how: Reads active evidence quotes with no stored translation, optionally for one industry. Detects each quote's language, skips English, already translated and repeated quotes, then prints a line per quote or JSON, followed by a count on the error output.
inputs: An optional industry name and an optional json flag.
outputs: Tab-separated lines or JSON on standard output, and a count message.
risks: Language detection is an estimate from the text, so a wrong guess gives a wrong list. Read-only, but it exits with success even when the list is empty.
debug: If nothing prints, check the spelling of the industry name. If a wrong language appears, look at quoteLanguage. If a duplicate appears, look at quoteKey.
